introHtml: course 2, week 1 on the audit page is 17 videos and 140 minutes, plus practice quizzes and three ungraded labs. It is not on YouTube. Last week's forward pass by hand already gave 0.527, so this week turns that into code: loops, matrices, Keras, and counting parameters. Read Chapter 14 of the notes before the videos each day; it already has the forward pass and a new section called "Layer by layer in code", tested on 27 Oct.

days.label: Monday 26 Oct
days.html:
ML 1 of 3: what a layer is (6 videos, 49 minutes)

  • Open the course page and check that week 1 opens.
  • Hands first: from memory, write what one neuron computes (z = w·x + b, then the activation), then a layer of 3 neurons with the weights in a matrix W of shape (n, units).
  • Read Chapter 14 of the notes up to the new section.
  • Watch course 2, week 1, videos 1 and 3 to 7:
# Video Length
1 Welcome! 3
3 Demand Prediction 16
4 Example: Recognizing Images 7
5 Neural network layer 10
6 More complex neural networks 8
7 Inference: making predictions (forward propagation) 5
  • Drill, agent off, 25 minutes: write dense_loop(a_in, W, b, g) that loops over the units one at a time, and use it twice on x = [2, 1]. First layer: W = [[1, 0.5], [-1, 0.5]] (column j holds the weights of unit j), b = [0, -1], sigmoid. Second layer: W = [[1], [-1]], b = [0]. You should get hidden values 0.731 and 0.622, and an output of 0.527, the same as the paper drill of last week.

Done when: your loop gives 0.527 and you can say in one sentence what a layer is and what its output is for the next layer.

days.label: Tuesday 27 Oct
days.html:
ML 2 of 3: neural networks in code (5 videos, 39 minutes, and one lab)

  • Hands first: from memory, the shapes. A batch X has m rows and n columns; W has n rows and units columns; b has units numbers. What shape is X @ W + b?
  • Read the new Chapter 14 section "Layer by layer in code". Then watch:
# Video Length
8 Inference in Code 7
9 Data in TensorFlow 11
10 Building a neural network 8
11 Forward prop in a single layer 5
12 General implementation of forward propagation 8
  • 15 minutes: skim the Keras guide The Sequential model and the Dense layer page. Note what Dense(units, activation=...) creates and what set_weights expects.
  • Drill, agent off, 25 minutes: build the same network as yesterday in Keras (keras.Sequential, two Dense layers, sigmoid), load yesterday's W and b with layer.set_weights([W, b]), and predict on x = [2, 1]. You should get 0.527 again, and model.count_params() should say 9.
  • 15 minutes: run the ungraded lab "Coffee Roasting in Tensorflow" on the audit page from top to bottom without editing it. Write one line: where does the data get scaled, and why?
  • Write a line in progress-log.md for the drill.

Done when: Keras prints 0.527 and 9, and you can explain why the loop version, the matrix version and Keras give the same number.

days.label: Wednesday 28 Oct
days.html:
ML 3 of 3: matrices, and course 2 week 1 on one page (5 videos, 40 minutes)

  • Hands first: count the parameters of a network with 2 inputs, 3 hidden units and 1 output. Each unit has one weight per input plus one bias.
  • Read the part of Chapter 14 on parameters and the part of Chapter 7 on vectorization. Then watch:
# Video Length
2 Neurons and the brain 11
14 How neural networks are implemented efficiently 4
15 Matrix multiplication 9
16 Matrix multiplication rules 10
17 Matrix multiplication code 6
  • Optional: 3Blue1Brown, Matrix multiplication as composition, the picture behind A @ W.
  • Drill, agent off, 20 minutes: count parameters by hand for 2-3-1 (answer 13) and for Ng's digit network 400-25-15-1 (answer 10,025 + 390 + 16 = 10,431). Then build the 400-25-15-1 model in Keras and check that model.summary() agrees. In your own words, why does the first layer hold almost all of them?
  • 25 minutes: the ungraded lab "CoffeeRoastingNumPy". It is yesterday's dense function in a real example.
  • 15 minutes, agent off: course 2, week 1 on one page, from memory, in 8 lines: neuron, layer, activation, forward propagation, Dense, Sequential, parameter count, matrix multiplication. Then compare with Chapter 14 and fix what you got wrong.

Done when: you have both parameter counts, and the one-page summary has 8 lines. The practice quizzes and video 13 ("Is there a path to AGI?", 11 minutes) go in Thursday's hour.

Fallback if the audit is blocked: do the same three days with Chapter 14, the Keras guide, 3Blue1Brown chapters 3 and 4 (backpropagation, a week early), and the drills above, which need no course access.

doneHtml:
• ML: the layer loop gives 0.731, 0.622 and 0.527; Keras gives 0.527 with 9 parameters; the parameter counts 13 and 10,431 by hand; the one-page summary of course 2 week 1 with 8 lines; two week 1 quizzes done by Thursday.
  • Course 2: week 1 of the audit opens.
